claims: VA home loans are backed by the Department of Veterans Affairs.
VA home loans are issued by private lenders.
VA home loans can be used to purchase homes.
VA home loans can be used to build homes.
VA home loans can be used to refinance homes.
A Certificate of Eligibility (COE) is required to show qualification for VA home loans.
No down payment is required in most cases for VA home loans provided the sales price does not exceed the appraised value.
No Private Mortgage Insurance (PMI) is required for VA home loans.
The Department of Veterans Affairs limits the fees and closing costs that veterans can pay.
VA home loans generally have lower interest rates than traditional conventional or FHA loans.
VA home loan eligibility for wartime requires 90 consecutive days of active duty.
VA home loan eligibility for peacetime requires 181 consecutive days of active duty.
VA home loan eligibility for Guard/Reserve requires 6 years or 90 days under Title 32 orders (at least 30 consecutive days).
Certain surviving spouses of veterans who died in service or from service-connected disabilities are eligible for VA home loans.
VA Purchase Loans are used to buy a home.
VA Cash-Out Refinance loans are used to refinance a non-VA loan or cash out equity.
Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) is also called a VA streamline.
Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) is used to lower the interest rate on an existing VA loan.
Native American Direct Loan (NADL) is for Native American veterans buying or building on federal trust land.
Eligible recipients of VA home loans include veterans, service members, and surviving spouses.
